reason: Reviewed the complete assigned inventory, approved OPT6 contract, current supplier claims and proofs, and page interfaces. Three defects can be addressed locally on the A page: the globalization SOC call is underspecified, its accepted outputs and domain-exit status omit approved scope, and the augmented-Lagrangian method has no finite inner budget.

findings.reason: The SOC call does not specify which constraint map c_A to correct or supply it. The exact QP solver returns J but this algorithm discards it and does not identify the retained independent equality rows. It also calls SOC without ensuring x+p is in U, a stated SOC precondition. Retain J and the deterministic independent equality basis, pass c_A=(h_E,g_J), and skip SOC when x+p is outside U.

The approved OPT6 contract requires accepted steps to take the QP multipliers and treats domain exit separately. Both accepted branches currently return only a point or fraction, and if all ordinary trials are outside U they are folded into line-search-budget-exhausted. Return the QP multiplier data on acceptance and add a distinct domain-exit status when no trial can be evaluated in-domain.

The approved OPT6 contract requires finite inner and outer budgets. This method caps only outer iterations; its inner oracle has no stated cap or finite-call condition, although the proof asserts each call is finite. Specify a finite inner budget and an explicit exhaustion result carrying the reported residual or failure data.
